CONCEPT: a citizen of the Hydrogen Nation, of the Oil House. A female personification character with a Victorian street gas lamp — a cast-iron post with a glass lantern head and a glowing white mantle as her motif — the object reimagined as a woman in cloth and ornament that carry its materials, colors, shape and motifs. She does NOT hold, carry or wield the object; it is not a separate object. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing.
ELEMENT TRAITS of Hydrogen (H) to carry in her design and the scene: airy, pale and luminous, always rising: translucent layers, upward-drifting hair and hems, a faint pale-blue flame (hydrogen burns almost invisibly), star-light and fusion white, water droplets and mist; it is the lightest element, the fuel of stars and half of every drop of water. Palette: pale sky blue, white, silver, a faint violet flame, clear glass.
HOUSE TRAITS of Oil: hydrocarbons as the light locked inside: pale paraffin wax, clean gaslight flames, rising heat shimmer, glowing mantles and soft candlelight; creamy whites and pale golds with clear blue gas flames; the light, luminous side of hydrogen. Palette: wax cream, candle gold, gas-flame blue, warm white.
AGE: mid-twenties — a clear adult face; no facial lines.
SILHOUETTE: statuesque, long-legged, with a natural neck length build; long straight hair with side-swept bangs; white-blue plasma-bright hair.
FACE — she must read as her own person at a glance, NOT the style's default pretty face and not a sister of the other characters: first impression — a cool, aloof beauty; olive skin; long face; smaller, narrower eyes than usual anime proportion — narrow upturned eyes, outer eye corners tilting sharply upward; thick straight brows; aquiline nose; thin long lips; gold eyes; sharp winged eyeliner.
WORLD — STEAMPUNK: around 1900, an airship harbour: great hydrogen gas envelopes under a mooring mast, brass valves and gauges, an electrolysis laboratory with glass jars and a spectroscope, telegraph wires, dawn haze. COSTUME (citizen, steampunk): her object leads — its silhouette, parts and materials must read at first glance in her outfit and headpiece, the object reimagined as cloth, leather and brass fittings; the steampunk era only sets the late-Victorian cut and the brass-and-leather finish. Steam, pipes and gauges in the scene; no modern plastic, no sci-fi. LIGHT: hazy gaslight and a smoky overcast sky, unless TIME & WEATHER says otherwise. HAIR: her hair is worn exactly as SILHOUETTE says — loose, long or cut as named; do not pin it up into a bun or tuck it under goggles or a hat unless SILHOUETTE says an updo.
STYLE: Polished 2.5D game key art with clean linework, anime facial design that keeps each character's own facial structure, eye proportions and skin tone instead of one house face, layered cel-to-soft shading and crisp costume and prop detail. Use a vivid, readable silhouette and campaign-quality lighting.
EXPOSURE (bold): her outfit opens to show skin — a deep open neckline with natural cleavage, bare shoulders or arms, a high slit or a short hem where the outfit allows; pieces stay symmetrical. Nothing slipped off. Chest and pelvis covered; no corset; keep the object's shape, material and palette.
OUTPUT: one character image that works as card art. Vertical 2:3 frame, full body with head and feet inside the frame with clear margins, face turned toward the camera (front or three-quarter). Standing, card-ready pose; the environment may be rich while her design stays fully readable.
EXPRESSION: relaxed brow, softly open eyes, lips closed and unstrained, no smile.
BODY: a normal human body — one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint. Hands and feet may be partly hidden by the pose or the frame.
ONE FIGURE ONLY. No second character, no living creature, no logo, no watermark, no speech bubble, no frame border. No text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (H) and atomic number (1) — those two may appear readably (engraved, stamped, glowing or on a sign or label); nothing else is written.
ANATOMY: natural adult proportions, both hands drawn correctly as hands. No extra limbs.
